England.difference_en: England introduces factor pairs in Year 4 and systematically finds all factors and common factors in Year 5. China's third learning stage includes factors, common factors and greatest common factors.
England.why_en: Factors are clearer when linked to multiplication structures rather than learned only as a definition.
England.classroom_use_en: Build different rectangular arrays for 24 and read a factor pair from each array.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 4 requires all factor pairs for whole numbers from 1-100 and explicitly develops the factor-multiple relationship.
US.why_en: Factor understanding grows directly from multiplication relationships and supports prime/composite work.
US.classroom_use_en: Whenever stating that 6 is a factor of 24, also write 6×4=24.

England.difference_en: England Year 5 identifies multiples and Year 6 uses common multiples in number and fraction work. China's third learning stage includes multiples, common multiples and least common multiples.
England.why_en: Multiples extend a number through whole-number scaling and reverse the direction of the factor relationship.
England.classroom_use_en: Contrast '6 is a factor of 24' with '24 is a multiple of 6'.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 4 identifies multiples of one-digit numbers; Grade 6 uses least common multiples.
US.why_en: Multiple structure extends multiplication facts into common cycles and denominator work.
US.classroom_use_en: Mark multiples of 6 and 8 on a number line and find the first common point.

England.difference_en: England Year 5 uses the vocabulary of prime, prime factor and composite and identifies primes within 100. China's third learning stage also formally includes prime and composite numbers.
England.why_en: Prime classification comes from factor structure, not from being odd.
England.classroom_use_en: Use arrays to test 9, 11 and 13 and classify them from their factors.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 4 determines whether whole numbers from 1-100 are prime or composite.
US.why_en: This content is built directly on Grade 4 factor-pair work.
US.classroom_use_en: Find all factors before naming a number prime or composite, and discuss 1 separately.

England.difference_en: England Years 5-6 use common factors and common multiples, including fraction simplification and common-denominator work. China's third learning stage explicitly includes greatest common factors and least common multiples.
England.why_en: Common factors answer grouping/divisibility questions; common multiples answer questions about when multiple sequences meet.
England.classroom_use_en: Contrast a 'largest equal group' problem with a 'first time both repeat together' problem before choosing GCF or LCM.

US.difference_en: Common Core Grade 6 explicitly requires greatest common factors and least common multiples within stated ranges.
US.why_en: The progression extends factor/multiple reasoning from one number to relationships between two numbers.
US.classroom_use_en: Identify the problem structure before applying a GCF or LCM procedure.
